title: Choose rounding mode when casting to dtype
github_labels: module: cuda|triaged|module: type promotion|function request|oncall: pt2|module: inductor|module: floatx (formerly float8)|bot-triaged
body_excerpt: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `tensor.to(dtype)` performs a round-nearest conversion. This makes sense in most cases, but there are situations where other rounding modes are useful. For example in MXFP8 (microscaled float8) on Blackwell GPUs, we need to convert the scales to their next power of 2 and convert them to a float8_e8m0fnu (i.e., a biased uint8). This could be done in one shot via `scales.to(torch.float8_e8m0fnu, round="up")`. Which then would allow PyTorch to match this exactly to the optimized PTX instruction `cvt.rp.satfinite.ue8m0x2.f32` (`.rp` means round-positive). ### Alternatives Several less-readable alternatives, which will also make it harder for PyTorch and Inductor to understand the intent and thus optimize the code. For example one could go through torch.log and torch.ceil, or through torch.frexp, or do the cast with round-nearest and the conditionally adjust the result. ### Additional context _No response_ cc @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @jerryzh168 @tinglvv @nWEIdia @nairbv @mruberry @voznesenskym @penguinwu @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @ipiszy @kadeng @muchulee8 @amjames @chauhang @aak...

title: [BUG] Consider disabling managed memory in cudf.pandas on WSL2
body_excerpt: **Describe the bug** cudf.pandas turns on a managed pool allocator by default to support larger-than-memory workloads. However, this does not work on WSL2 because UVM on Windows does not actually allow oversubscription. Moreover, using UVM could result in far worse slowdowns on WSL2 than observed on Windows due to how it is implemented on that platform.  **Expected behavior** We should consider changing cudf.pandas to only enable managed memory by default when oversubscription is properly supported. This can be done by querying the CUDA driver for the appropriate attribute. In addition, we should run some benchmarks to evaluate the relative performance impact of using managed memory on WSL2 in undersubscribed situations

title: [TASK] Increase parallelism or sparse normalization prims
body_excerpt: Cuml has CSR-based primitives that contain kernels, both in Python and in C, which currently map each row of the CSR to a single thread and loop over the columns serially to perform L1/l2/l_inf normalization. The performance and the parallelism, including the sums, could be made much more parallel if we map the individual rows to warps with a block size set to something like the average degree. The current method might be the best option when the average degree is extremely small but as the average degree grows larger, the parallelism can be increased significantly, while also enabling coalesced reads (and potentially even writes in the case of normalization where all the values need to be modified).

title: [RFC] Improving Coalescing and Layout Propagation
body_excerpt: ## Motivation The following work is done jointly by me and my team @kaitingwang at Huawei Canada. The TritonGPUCoalesce pass generates blocked layouts for load/stores that favour memory coalescing and vectorization. body_excerpt: This issue serves as a backup of some ideas discussed in the Gitter room. # Result caching in combination with Numba ## Premise One clear application of numba is the speedup of costly computations. Besides acceleration of such computations, it could be useful to cache results of such functions, if they are pure functions and expected to be called with the same parameters frequently. body_excerpt: Using NN Descent to build the knn graph for UMAP and HDBSCAN is working okay, but a few improvements can be made. Related PRs: - HDBSCAN + NN Descent [here](https://github.com/rapidsai/cuml/pull/5939) - UMAP + NN Descent [here](https://github.com/rapidsai/cuml/pull/5910) **[Precision Issues with NN Descent]** NN Descent in RAFT uses fp16 to calculate distances. This makes it difficult to grab the distances calculated by NN Descent and compare it against fp32-calculated distances for additional operations outside of NN Descent such as making predictions.
